abstract: Reversible solid oxide cells (r‐SOCs) are promising technologies for integrating intermittent renewable electricity with hydrogen production and storage, and their performance strongly depends on fuel‐electrode design. title: Extending a <mark>Thermal Runaway</mark> Modeling Framework to Cells of Different Formats, Sizes, and Chemistries
authors: Nikola Vujnović, Karl Hohenberg, Patrick Höschele and Christian Ellersdorfer
abstract: Simplified staged <mark>thermal runaway</mark> (TR) models are attractive for early-stage battery safety assessment, but they are usually parameterized for a single cell type and rely on internal temperature measurements that are impractical in sealed cylindrical and pouch cells. This work extends a four-stage TR modeling framework so it can be applied to cylindrical and pouch cells of different sizes with nickel-rich layered-oxide cathodes using surface-temperature data from accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) alone.
